summary: Defines a new WebDAV property that lets a client quickly find the principal that corresponds to the currently authenticated user. This is a Proposed Standard.

eli5.summary: When you log in to a shared folder, the server can quickly tell you who it thinks you are, so you do not have to hunt for your own name tag.

questions: how to find the current user in webdav
subtitle: A WebDAV property that tells a client which principal resource represents the user it is logged in as.

tldr.problem: WebDAV ACL clients had no recommended way to learn which principal the server associates with the authenticated user, and the principal-match REPORT can return the user plus every group the user belongs to without saying which is which.
tldr.mechanism: The new DAV:current-user-principal property holds a single DAV:href URL to the user's principal resource, or DAV:unauthenticated when nobody is authenticated.
tldr.outcome: A client can use that URL to bootstrap further queries on the principal resource, such as group membership.

today: RFC 5397 is a Proposed Standard, and no later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why a Client Needs Its Own Principal
sections.content:
WebDAV (RFC 4918) extends HTTP for document authoring, and WebDAV ACL (RFC 3744) adds access control and the idea of a principal resource that represents an authenticated entity. A client often needs to know which principal the server ties to the current HTTP user, for example to see which groups the user is in or to change a property of the user's own principal.

RFC 3744 defines DAV:current-user-privilege-set but no way to name the principal itself. The DAV:principal-match REPORT is ambiguous, because it returns the user principal and every group principal the user belongs to, with no clear way to tell them apart.
sections.eli5: You can ask a server what you are allowed to do, but not easily who it thinks you are. This fixes that.

sections.title: The current-user-principal Property
sections.content:
The property DAV:current-user-principal lives in the DAV: namespace and is protected, because it is computed on every request. Its value is a single DAV:href or a DAV:unauthenticated element.

The URL MUST be one of the URLs in the principal resource's DAV:principal-URL or DAV:alternate-URI-set properties, and MUST use an http or https scheme. If authentication has not been done or has failed, the property MUST contain the DAV:unauthenticated pseudo-principal.

It is never copied or moved. Only one URL is allowed; a client that wants alternates can query the principal resource itself.
sections.eli5: The server answers with one web address that points to your own page, or says you are not logged in.

sections.title: Choosing a URL and an Example
sections.content:
Several principal resource URLs may refer to the same principal. In that case the server is free to choose any one of them, but SHOULD be consistent and use the same URL for each authenticated principal.

The RFC's example returns /principals/users/cdaboo inside a DAV:href element. The document introduces no security issues beyond those of HTTP, WebDAV and WebDAV ACL.
sections.eli5: If you have several name tags, the server picks the same one for you every time.
